main_text.head: CAP. VII.
Propriam & primariam significationem Græcæ vocis, εἰδωλον, à Bellarmino perversissimè ad commenti sui defensionem torqueri.
Bellarminus.
main_text.p: Eod.lib.2. cap. 5.tom.1 con-trovers.7.QUinto[?], ex ipsa vocis proprietate; nam (ut Tertullianus docet libro de ido-lolatria) idolum est diminutivum ab εἶδος, id est, forma, & significat formam parvam, non quantitate sola, sed perfectione, est enim proprie idolum (ut exponit Eustathius in libro II. Odysseæ) imago inanis, qualis est, quæ cernitur in umbra hominis, & qualia sunt phantasmata, id est, imagines quas imaginatione fabricamus, quibus sæpe nihil respondet in re; & qualia denique sunt spectra & umbra mortuorum, quæ videntur quidem esse aliquid solidum, sed inanes sunt. Unde Homerus in II. Odysseæ, & Lucianus in Dialogo de mortuis, animas mortuorum vocat εἰδωλα. & Virgilius in sexto libro Æneidos videtur idipsum explicare voluisse, cùm ait:

Corripit hic subita trepidus formidine ferrum Æneas, strictamq; aciem venientibus offert: Et, ni docta comes tenues sine corpore vitas Admoneat volitare cava sub imagine formæ; Irruat, & frustra ferro diverberet umbras.

p.i: Vbi quod Homerus, et Lucianus vocant εἰδωλα, vo-cat ipse umbras, & cavas imagines, id est, vanas & inanes.

page.notes: Woodcut initial read as Q, probably "Quinto"; the printed letter is ornate and only partly clear, so marked [?]. Right-aligned final paragraph is italic. Verse stanza is one paragraph with line breaks. Greek words (εἶδος, εἰδωλον, εἰδωλα) are transcribed as read in the scan and may need checking at accents. The Roman numeral "II." appears as "11." in the scan and is read as II. Head "Bellarminus." is set as a level 2 head.
